This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 20 Aug '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MET Malaysia) currently indicate a maximum of 34°C for Kuala Lumpur on August 21, 2026, with isolated afternoon thunderstorms expected.** This aligns closely with the market’s leading implied probabilities for 34°C (48.0%) and 33°C (36.5%), reflecting trader consensus around typical late-August conditions during the southwest monsoon.

Kuala Lumpur’s tropical equatorial climate features consistent daytime highs near 32–34°C in August, moderated by high humidity, cloud cover, and convective rainfall that often peaks in the afternoon and can suppress peak temperatures if storms develop early. Recent MET Malaysia updates and international guidance (including Met Office and AccuWeather outlooks) show no significant heat anomaly or clear-sky persistence that would push readings to 35°C or above, keeping those outcomes at much lower implied odds (10.5% and below). 

Urban heat-island effects around the official recording station and steering patterns favoring brief thundershowers remain the primary variables that could shift the realized maximum between 33°C and 34°C. Updated model runs and any revisions to the afternoon thunderstorm timing over the next 48 hours represent the key upcoming data points likely to influence positioning before resolution.
